source_en: The fourth layer (L4: Executable—reference applications and services) focuses on software applications and services within a digital ecosystem. It is intended to include executable reference software that accurately represents the intentions, operational, and functional requirements of the WHO recommendations; addresses user and health system needs; and comprises machine-readable data and calculations within interoperability standards, as documented in the L1–L3 layers. As a fully functional application, it is intended to serve as a generic starting point, ready to be localised to the specific operational context of the users, population, and health system within which it is deployed. Additional products at this layer include terminology services to support consistent data representation for interoperability; reusable software libraries including software development kits; application programming interfaces; and function as a service to support updates to FHIR content and capabilities across subscribed digital systems.
back_translation_en: The fourth level (L4: executable — reference applications and services) concerns software applications and services within a digital ecosystem. It is intended to comprise executable reference software that faithfully represents the operational and functional intentions and requirements of WHO recommendations; that meets the needs of users and the health system; and that includes machine-readable data and calculations conforming to interoperability standards, as documented at levels L1 to L3. As a fully functional application, it is intended to serve as a generic starting point, ready to be adapted to the specific operational context of the users, the population and the health system in which it is deployed. The other products at this level include terminology services promoting consistent data representation for interoperability; reusable software libraries, including software development kits; application programming interfaces; and functions as a service to support updates to FHIR content and capabilities across all subscribed digital systems.

source_en: The standards-based technical artifacts in this implementation guide are at the third layer of knowledge representation (L3: Machine-readable recommendations). It provides code necessary for software developers to incorporate standardised logic from WHO guidelines into digital systems, testable for conformance to standards including fidelity to recommendations. A standards-based technical implementation guide builds on operational (L2) by mapping L2 content to value sets and Health Level Seven International Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) standards. Alongside data standards from L2, this allows for semantic and syntactic interoperability at scale. The logic derived from guidelines, which might include clinical decision support and calculations for performance indicators, which may be encoded into Clinical Quality Language (CQL). This ensures that key indicators can be consistently extracted to support patient care, as well as case surveillance and programme monitoring. The machine-readable representations in this implementation guide are intended for adaptation into countries’ digital health service delivery and reporting systems. Digital solutions comprising L3 machine-readable recommendations may then be testable for conformance to interoperability standards.
back_translation_en: The standards-based technical artifacts of this implementation guide sit at the third level of knowledge representation (L3: machine-readable recommendations). It provides the code needed by software developers to integrate into digital systems standardized logic derived from WHO guidelines, whose conformance to standards, including fidelity to the recommendations, can be tested. A standards-based technical implementation guide builds on the operational level (L2) by mapping L2 content to value sets and to the FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) standards of Health Level Seven International. Combined with the data standards of level L2, this enables semantic and syntactic interoperability at scale. Logic derived from the guidelines, which may include clinical decision support and performance indicator calculations, can be encoded in Clinical Quality Language (CQL). This ensures that key indicators can be extracted consistently to support patient care, as well as case surveillance and programme monitoring. The machine-readable representations of this implementation guide are intended to be adapted to national digital health service delivery and reporting systems. Digital solutions incorporating level L3 machine-readable recommendations can then be tested for their conformance to interoperability standards.

source_en: WHO guidelines articulate and endorse rigorously tested recommendations for health interventions to be adopted within country programs. When applied correctly and consistently, guideline recommendations save lives. To ensure that countries can effectively benefit from digital health investments, the SMART Guidelines approach is intended to facilitate the accurate reflection of WHO’s clinical, public health and data use guidelines in the digital systems that countries are adopting.
back_translation_en: WHO guidelines formulate and approve rigorously tested recommendations concerning the health interventions to be adopted in national programmes. Applied correctly and consistently, the guideline recommendations save lives. So that countries can take full advantage of investments in digital health, the SMART guidelines approach aims to facilitate the faithful transposition of WHO clinical, public health and data use guidelines into the digital systems that countries adopt.

source_en: A digital document that contains essential healthcare information about a patient, designed to support the continuity of care and patient safety. For Hajj pilgrims, the IPS includes basic demographics, medical history, medications, allergies, and other critical health information that can be shared across borders and healthcare systems.
back_translation_en: Digital document containing a patient's essential health information, designed to promote continuity of care and patient safety. For Hajj pilgrims, the IPS includes basic demographic data, medical history, medications, allergies and other essential health information that can be shared across borders and between health systems.

source_en: A digital version of a patient's paper chart, used by healthcare providers for diagnosis and treatment. In the context of the Hajj, EMRs are used by host country medical facilities to manage pilgrim care.
back_translation_en: Digital version of a patient's paper record, used by health care providers for diagnosis and treatment. In the Hajj context, EMRs are used by the medical facilities of the host country to manage the care of pilgrims.

source_en: A healthcare professional responsible for the initial registration of pilgrims at Hajj health facilities. This includes collecting and verifying pilgrim information and initiating the health service process.
back_translation_en: Health professional responsible for the initial registration of pilgrims at Hajj health facilities. This includes collecting and verifying the pilgrim's information and initiating the health service delivery process.

source_en: A machine-readable optical label that contains information about the item to which it is attached. In this context, it holds encrypted data that allows healthcare providers access to a pilgrim's IPS when scanned.
back_translation_en: Machine-readable optical label containing information about the item to which it is attached. In this context, it contains encrypted data that allow health care providers to access a pilgrim's IPS when it is scanned.

source_en: A medical facility set up to cater specifically to the needs of Hajj pilgrims. These facilities can range from clinics to hospitals and are equipped to handle both routine health checks and emergency services.
back_translation_en: Medical facility set up specifically to meet the needs of Hajj pilgrims. These facilities range from clinics to hospitals and are equipped to provide both routine health checks and emergency services.

source_en: A medical professional, such as a doctor or nurse, who provides clinical care to the pilgrim. Clinicians use the pilgrim's health information, accessed via the healthcare system, to offer appropriate medical treatments.
back_translation_en: Medical professional, such as a doctor or a nurse, who provides clinical care to the pilgrim. Clinicians use the pilgrim's health information, accessed through the health system, to offer appropriate medical treatments.

source_en: A person who undertakes the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca. In the context of the healthcare system, the pilgrim is the primary user, receiving healthcare services and interacting with various healthcare providers.
back_translation_en: Person who performs the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca. In the context of the health system, the pilgrim is the main user: they receive health services and interact with different health care providers.

source_en: A security feature that adds an extra layer of protection to the pilgrim's health information. The default PIN is often the pilgrim's birthdate, and it is used in conjunction with the QR code to access the IPS.
back_translation_en: Security feature that adds an additional level of protection to the pilgrim's health information. The default PIN is often the pilgrim's date of birth; it is used together with the QR code to access the IPS.

source_en: A Smart Health Link is a special link that provides time-bound, password and cryptographically restricted access to a health certificate or document.
back_translation_en: A Smart Health Link is a special link that gives time-limited, password-protected and cryptographically restricted access to a health certificate or a document.

source_en: An IPS document together with a digital signature that can be used to verify the provenance of the IPS within a Trust Network.
back_translation_en: IPS document accompanied by a digital signature making it possible to verify the provenance of the IPS within a trust network.

source_en: Tabung Haji is the Malaysian Hajj Pilgrims Fund Board, a government-linked financial institution that manages the savings of Muslims in Malaysia intending to perform the Hajj pilgrimage. It provides comprehensive services to pilgrims, including savings schemes, training, logistics, and healthcare services during the Hajj. Tabung Haji works closely with MOH to ensure the well-being of pilgrims, particularly in health-related matters.
back_translation_en: Tabung Haji is the Pilgrims Fund Board of Malaysia, a government-linked financial institution that manages the savings of Malaysian Muslims wishing to perform the Hajj pilgrimage. It provides comprehensive services to pilgrims, including savings plans, training, logistics and health services during the Hajj. Tabung Haji works closely with the MOH to ensure the well-being of pilgrims, particularly for health matters.

source_en: The Hajj Health Examination is a comprehensive medical check-up conducted for Malaysian Hajj pilgrims. This examination is a mandatory requirement to ensure that pilgrims are fit for the journey and to identify any underlying health conditions that need to be managed during the Hajj. The examination includes general health assessments, vaccinations, and screenings for infectious diseases. The data from these examinations are recorded in a FHIR compliant electronic medical record (EMR) system called MyVAS and made accessible to pilgrims instantaneously through the MySejahtera app.
back_translation_en: The Hajj health examination is a comprehensive medical check-up carried out for Malaysian Hajj pilgrims. This examination is a mandatory requirement aimed at ensuring that pilgrims are fit to travel and at identifying any underlying condition that needs to be managed during the Hajj. The examination includes general health assessments, vaccinations and infectious disease screenings. The data from these examinations are recorded in a FHIR-compliant electronic medical record (EMR) system called MyVAS and made instantly available to pilgrims via the MySejahtera application.

source_en: The health records in this implementation are based on the Hajj Pilgrims Health Examination program conducted for Malaysian Hajj pilgrims. These examinations are conducted by the MOH health facilities and empanelled private general practitioners (GPs) by Tabung Haji across Malaysia.
back_translation_en: The health records of this implementation are based on the Hajj pilgrim health examination programme conducted for Malaysian Hajj pilgrims. These examinations are carried out by MOH health facilities and by private general practitioners approved by Tabung Haji throughout Malaysia.

source_en: The Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) is the government ministry responsible for the health system in Malaysia. MOH is dedicated to improving the health of the population through comprehensive health services, promotion of health awareness, and ensuring access to quality healthcare. The ministry plays a crucial role in implementing health policies, conducting health examinations, and collaborating on international health initiatives.
back_translation_en: The Ministry of Health of Malaysia (MOH) is the government ministry responsible for the health system in Malaysia. The MOH works to improve the health of the population through comprehensive health services, promoting health awareness and ensuring access to quality care. The ministry plays an essential role in implementing health policies, carrying out health examinations and collaborating on international health initiatives.

source_en: The primary objective of this implementation is to enable Malaysian pilgrims traveling to Saudi Arabia for this year’s Hajj to carry their health records on the MySejahtera app as a Smart Health Certificate QR on the Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN). In the event of an unexpected medical episode, healthcare professionals in Saudi Arabia can scan the QR code, access the medical history, and treat the patients appropriately.
back_translation_en: The main objective of this implementation is to allow Malaysian pilgrims travelling to Saudi Arabia for this year's Hajj to carry their health records on the MySejahtera application in the form of a Smart Health Certificate QR code on the Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN). In the event of an unexpected medical episode, health professionals in Saudi Arabia can scan the QR code, access the medical history and treat patients appropriately.

The use of standardized health records and QR codes ensures that healthcare providers can quickly access essential medical information, facilitating timely and effective medical care during the Hajj.

The use of standardized health records and QR codes ensures that health care providers can quickly access essential medical information, facilitating rapid and effective medical care during the Hajj.
